ja: ריקם, וקאל אל תאמר כאשר עשה לי כן אעשה לו, וקאל אואילנא ע"ס הנעלבים ואינם עולבים שומעים חרפתם ואינם משיבים עושים מאהבה ושמחים ביסורין עליהם הכתוב אומר ואוהביו כצאת השמש בגבורתו, והו אלמסמי ענדהם מעביר על מדותיו. ואלראבעה פעל אלג'מיל פי אלנאס וחסן אלקול פיהם, ואלאעד'אר ענהם, ותרך אלגיבה ואלוקיעה פיהם, ותחליל גיבתה ווקיעתה להם ואן לם יסתחקוא ד'לך מנה, כקולה גם במדעך מלך אל תקלל, וקאל פיך שלחת ברעה וגו' תשב באחיך תדבר בבן אמך תתן דופי, ופי תחליל אלגיבה ואלוקיעה קול אלכתאב ותדבר מרים ואהרן במשה, פקאל והאיש משה ענו מאד למא סמח להמא. ומן ד'לך קול אלחכים איצ'א גם לכל הדברים אשר ידברו אל תתן לבך אשר לא תשמע את עבדך מקללך, כי גם פעמים רבות ידע לבך אשר גם אתה קללת אחרים. וקאלוא אואילנא מעשה ברבי אליעזר שירד לפני התיבה ואמר עשרים וארבע רננות ולא נענה, ירד ר' עקיבה ואמר אבינו מלכנו אין לנו אלא אתה אבינו מלכנו רחם עלינו ונענה, יצאה בת קול ואמרה לא שזה גדול מזה, אלא שזה מעביר על מדותיו וזה אינו מעביר על מדותיו. וקד קיל ען בעץ' אלצאלחין אנה עבר פי טריקה עלי ג'יפהֵ כלב שדידהֵ אלראיחה, פקאל לה מן חצ'ר מן תלאמד'תה מא אשד נתן ראיחהֵ הד'ה אלג'יפה, פקאל להם מא אשד ביאץ' אסנאנהא, פכלחוא תלאמיד'ה למא תקדם להם מן קביח אלקול פיהא. פאד'א קבח סו אלקול פי ג'יפהֵ כלב אחרי פי אנסאן חי, ואד'א צלח אלתזיין עלי ג'יפהֵ כלב בביאץ' אסנאנהא פעלי חסב ד'לך ילזם אלתזיין עלי אלאנסאן אלד'י יפהם

**The fourth**: when he brings to mind what is binding upon him of obedience to God on account of His abundant bounty toward him and His lavish beneficence to him; his turning aside from the rational and the heard-revealed laws and his falling-short in them; the cutting-off of his case and the narrowing of excuses upon him on the day of the reckoning; and his regret in the standing of the requital — he humbles himself, is lowered, his soul is broken, as He said: "For behold, the day comes, burning like an oven, and all the proud and all the doers of wickedness shall be stubble; and the day that comes shall set them ablaze, says the Lord of hosts, that shall leave them neither root nor branch" (Malachi 3:19); and He said: "Who can endure the day of His coming, and who shall stand at His appearing? For He is like a refiner's fire and like fullers' soap" (Malachi 3:2).

**The fifth**: when he reflects on the majesty of the Creator (exalted be He) and the piercing of His power, the One who is overseeing his outer and his inner — and there falls into his soul this momentous matter, as the early ones mentioned of many of the excellent ones of preceding ages, of the awe and the majesty; so too their saying: "He set his eyes upon him and he became a heap of bones" (b. Berakhot 58a); and they said of Jonathan ben Uzziel: "When he expounded Torah, every bird that flew over him was burned up" (b. Sukkah 28a). There is no doubt that the rank of the prophets is above their rank; and you find the prophets — their strengths poured out, falling prostrate at their meeting with the angels — as in Daniel and Ezekiel and Joshua, and many like them. You find in the Truthful Book that the angels themselves fall prostrate to God (exalted be He), as He said: "And the host of heaven bows down to You" (Nehemiah 9:6); and He said: "Behold, in His servants He places no trust, and His angels He charges with imperfection" (Job 4:18); and He said: "And in His sanctuary all of it says: Glory!" (Psalms 29:9); and He said: "And one cried to another…" (Isaiah 6:3).

There is in what is manifest to our intellects from the side of His made things — like the sun and the moon and the stars and the celestial sphere and the earth and what is upon it of inanimate, plant, and animal — sufficiency for one who has understood and reasoned, as He said: "How great are Your works, O Lord — very deep are Your thoughts; the brutish man does not know, and the fool does not understand this" (Psalms 92:6–7); and He said: "All the nations are as nothing before Him" (Isaiah 40:17); and He said in the Targum: "All the inhabitants of the earth are as nothing reckoned." When the discerning, sharp man reflects on his proportion to the rational beings, and the proportion of the rational beings to the globe of the earth, and the proportion of the earth to the sphere of the moon, and the sphere of the moon to the highest sphere; and the totality of that, in the face of the power of the Creator (exalted be He), has no proportion and no measure — he sees the measure of the human, in the face of the power of the Creator, as nothing. He humbles himself within himself and is lowered before his Creator, as He said: "What is the human, that You remember him; the son of man, that You take note of him?" (Psalms 8:5).

**The sixth**: when he reads the Book of God and sees the severity of God's punishment and His threat to the people of magnification and self-glorification, and the intensity of His care for the humble and the lowered — he humbles himself and is lowered, as He said concerning the people of self-elevation and towering: "The lofty looks of man shall be brought low, and the haughtiness of men shall be bowed down; and the Lord alone shall be exalted on that day; for the day of the Lord of hosts shall be upon every proud and lofty one, and upon every lifted up and brought low" (Isaiah 2:11–12); and He said concerning the two ranks: "The Lord lifts up the humble, He brings down the wicked to the earth" (Psalms 147:6); and He said: "For the Lord is exalted, and sees the lowly" (Psalms 138:6); and He said concerning the humble: "And the humble shall inherit the land and shall delight in the abundance of peace" (Psalms 37:11); and: "Because the Lord has anointed Me to bring good news to the humble; He has sent Me to bind up the broken-hearted, to call to the captives liberty, and to those bound the opening of the prison; to call the year of the Lord's pleasure, and the day of vengeance" (Isaiah 61:1–2); and: "For thus says the lofty and exalted One, who dwells forever, whose name is Holy: I dwell on high and as the holy one — and with the crushed and the lowly of spirit" (Isaiah 57:15); and: "Before destruction is pride, and before stumbling is loftiness of spirit" (Proverbs 16:18).
